messages:
alex: Heads-up — over the past 30m we've seen a focused surge of spot evictions in us-west-2 for the g4dn-like pool. Low-tier latency SLOs are spiking and a few requests are hitting 503s when fallback routing doesn't kick fast enough.

mira: Yikes. Any pattern on instance age or specific zone?

alex: Mostly zone b and c. Median lifetime before eviction dropped from ~2h to ~18m after the batch jobs started. Also noticed our priority fanout currently fans to region fallback only after 45s. That's too slow for interactive.

devin: Suggestion: introduce hybrid routing that does two things: 1) immediate local soft-fail to a warm mixed pool (small reserved cushion) for p99 requests, 2) sub-2s cross-region spill for everything else. Keep costs controlled by throttling lower tiers and downgrading model variants first.

josh: +1. Operational sketch: warm pool = 3% of avg capacity pinned per region. If eviction rate > X then start draining lower-tier traffic to quantized variants (eg. redwood-1 -> redwood-1-q4) before routing across region.

mira: Can we codify that as a priority tree? Something like:
```yaml
routing_policy:
  - if region_health < 0.8:
      - route: warm_pool
      - downgrade: model_variant_q
      - if warm_pool_full: cross_region_fanout
  - else: normal
```
This keeps latency fast and limits cross-region egress.

devin: We'll need KPIs to decide thresholds: eviction_rate, local_p99_latency, warm_pool_fill, cross_region_rtt. I propose starting with eviction_rate > 0.05 over 5m window to trigger soft-fail and eviction_rate > 0.15 for full spillover.

alex: Cost tradeoffs: pinning a warm pool costs ~0.8% of monthly GPU spend for a 3% cushion, but reduces p99 latency spikes by ~30% in our sim. Downgrading to q4 reduces token cost ~45% at the expense of some quality regressions — should be limited to <10% of requests for paid tiers.

josh: For customer tiers: high-tier (enterprise) -> bypass downgrade, allow cross-region; mid-tier -> allow variant downgrade + warm pool; low-tier -> aggressive throttling + queued fallback or 204 degrade response. We should make this configurable per customer.

mira: Implementation notes: need a fast local health signal from kube node exporter + runtime eviction watcher. Routing decision should be done in the front proxy (edge) with a 200ms decision budget. Also add a circuit-breaker metric to avoid oscillation: once spilled, cool-down 60s unless region recovers.

devin: I'll prototype a greedy scheduler that picks warm slots from reserved pool and marks model-variant slots separately. Also add a "spill-score" telemetry field so we can backfill analytics and check for QoE regressions tied to downgrades.

alex: Can we run a 6h canary tomorrow: enable hybrid routing in us-west-2 beta for non-critical traffic (5% traffic) and collect cost + QoE delta?

josh: +1, schedule it. I'll attach a runbook.

sre-bot: deploy-bot: hybrid-routing canary started in us-west-2 (5% traffic) — canary id crn-2026-09-14-01

mira: Great. Devin — can you add two dashboards: 1) spill events + warm pool utilization, 2) QoE by model variant + customer tier. We need to watch for quality regressions fast.

devin: On it. I'll post the dashboards link once ready.

alex: Thanks all — main action items: prototype scheduler + routing rules, add metrics, run 6h canary, then reassess thresholds and cost windows. :thumbsup:
